decisions.reason: The source marker does not identify natural/artificial type, harmonic node, sounding pitch, or physical string/fret authority.
The notation proves technique provenance, but applying same-string or legato transition constraints would alter solver state and requires a separately approved physical contract.
Guitar Pro reuses the same numeric marker across chained start/start+stop/stop events, so number alone cannot establish physical transition identity.
Some corpus endpoints carry same-string position evidence while others do not. A global same-string or path constraint cannot be inferred from the producer form alone.
Natural/base-pitch source roles do not by themselves establish harmonic node or sounding-pitch transformation for the physical solver.
Base/touching/sounding pitch-role notes are explicit, but mapping those roles into solver note identity or string/fret state requires architectural semantics not proven by the current contract.
The per-note mute marker proves performance provenance but does not prove duration, scope, or a change to distinct-string physical occupancy.
The producer processing instruction does not prove sounding duration or deterministic termination scope.
